documents.exercise: A fictional project is expected to pay $100 in year one and $100 in year two with no additional payments. At an illustrative 10% annual discount rate, compute the present value.
documents.solution: The present value is 100/1.10 + 100/(1.10 squared), or approximately 90.91 + 82.64 = $173.55. The no-terminal-value assumption is intentionally artificial.
documents.counterexample: A small increase in long-run growth or decrease in discount rate can dramatically change a going-concern DCF; precise decimals do not remove uncertainty in forecasts.

documents.exercise: A fictional put has strike $60 and was purchased for $7 per underlying unit. At expiration the underlying is $55. Determine intrinsic payoff and premium-adjusted profit before fees.
documents.solution: Intrinsic payoff is max(60-55,0)=$5. Relative to the $7 paid, the result is -$2 per underlying unit before fees. A full loss of $7 is possible if it expires worthless.
documents.counterexample: A purchased put does not guarantee a positive net profit simply because the terminal stock price falls below strike; the premium can exceed intrinsic payout.
